Cathy left her friend at the restaurant to go to the residence of another male acquaintance who had invited her for a visit. She stated that she had to retrieve her purse from her friend's car and would be back in approximately half an hour. Cathy was reported missing by her mother on the morning of August 23, 1988. We have not had any further contact with Cathy.

Biogeographic Ancestry testing predicts this unidentified male is either of European ancestry, or South Asian ancestry, or mixed European and South Asian ancestry.

Teeth: Several amalgam fillings in his teeth and multiple posterior teeth in his upper and lower jaw were lost/removed prior to death.

It is believed that he was in the water for days to weeks prior to his discovery.

Case reference: 2014002108.CaseDesc: On August 18, 1978, Craig Waldum took part in a canoeing expedition along the Nelson River in Gillam, Manitoba, with seven other people. He was one of two guides on the trip. Three members of the group were on the riverbank. They were guiding the second canoe to shore with a rope. The remaining five members, including Craig, were in the second canoe. While guiding the canoe to shore, they gave the rope some slack. This caused the bow of the canoe to turn out into the current and tip over. Those on the shore were unable to hold onto the rope because of the strength of the current and the canoe was swept downstream. Craig held onto the canoe for a couple of hours, and then he was seen to let go. He slipped under the water and did not resurface. His remains have not been recovered.

Case reference: 2013000103.CaseDesc: Peter Bighetty was last seen on September 20, 1969 departing from Jackpine Island for Brochet Island via Reindeer Lake in Manitoba, with two fellow commercial fishermen. Peter was never seen again and his canoe was located in Reindeer Lake in a vertical position 9.6 kilometres south of Brochet, Manitoba. It is presumed Peter drowned and no foul play is suspected in this matter.

Case reference: 2014005000.CaseDesc: On August 10, 2004, Louis Lathlin was reported missing to police by his wife. She told police the last time she saw him was on June 14, when he left The Pas for Winnipeg, Manitoba for a doctor's appointment on the 15th. He took only personal hygiene items and no clothing. He later called his wife and told her that he would be staying in Winnipeg as he had another appointment on Thursday. He called his wife on Saturday morning requesting money. His wife sent the money as requested, but by Tuesday it had not been claimed. Louis has a history of living on the streets and has ties to Edmonton where he spent years on the streets. He also has various medical issues. He is believed to be in Winnipeg of his own volition. Louis' whereabouts remain unknown.

Case reference: 2015059939.CaseDesc: On October 20, 1973, the remains of a male were recovered from the water near the Fleet Street Pumping Station, Ottawa. His post-mortem weight was recorded as being between 170-180lbs, however, this measurement may not represent his actual living weight due to post-mortem changes noted at autopsy.
